text.p: Shares in Pioneer Electronic Corp fell on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on Tuesday morning amid a dearth of buying incentives after Monday's announcement of the April-June group earnings, brokers said.
As of 0130 GMT, the shares were down 50 yen to 2,740 yen.
The shares had surged last week on expectations of strong business results for the first quarter of fiscal 1997/98, which began on April 1.

Pioneer said on Monday it had a group pretax profit of 2.35 billion yen in the quarter, up from 766 million yen in the same period last year, and a group net profit of 1.03 billion yen versus 804 million yen.
All of Pioneer's divisions, except for the audio equipment division and the audio and video software division, marked higher sales.
Sales at Pioneer's audio equipment division fell 3.9 percent year-on-year, while the software division recorded a 42.1 percent drop.
